newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Media watchdog concerned at Bulgaria beatings.
newsitem.headline: Media watchdog concerned at Bulgaria beatings.

text.p: Paris-based press freedom watchdog Reporters sans Frontieres has written to Bulgaria's interior minister to express concern at attacks by police on journalists covering the siege of parliament on January 10 and 11.
Two photographers, a cameraman and two radio journalists were beaten by police using clubs to drive away protesters besieging the building in the early hours of Saturday.

"Our organisation asks you to stop police assaults on journalists and start an inquiry into this unacceptable violence," said the letter dated January 15, a copy of which was sent to Reuters on Thursday.
Three opposition deputies were also beaten during the demonstration.

Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev held a news conference on Wednesday at which he showed footage from police cameras and national television which showed protesters wrecking cars, throwing stones and breaking windows of the Grand Hotel Sofia, which is opposite the parliament.
He said police were working on identifying the people on the tapes and would arrest them.
Asked about the attacks on journalists and deputies, he said it was dark when riot police dispersed the crowd and no images were available.
He conceded that police had made some mistakes in the operation, which involved 2,500 members of the security forces.
"Police forces aren't very well equipped to cope with such a situation," Dobrev said.

He denied teargas had been used against protesters, and said fumes were caused by protesters' smoke bombs. Reporters who were inside and outside parliament on Friday night said teargas was fired from the second floor of the parliament.
"Throughout the whole incident we aimed to use minimum force to calm the clashes," he said.
A government statement said 196 people were treated in hospital. The opposition put the total number of injured much higher.
